title: Textual discovery revisions resurrect a retired endpoint in a durable snapshot
fault_primitive: Lexicographic journal replay followed by durable endpoint materialization shared by API and client readers
incident_class: Discovery snapshot migration applies retirement records out of order and commits a corrupt view at the correct high-water mark
symptoms: Intermittent hotel search failures with rate Unimplemented warnings. All application pods are Ready. Native Consul catalog and health responses identify the real rate server; the materialized discovery view also contains a retired endpoint now serving a different RPC capability.
why_hard: The correct catalog and correct revision watermark obscure the corrupt view. Revisions 9, 10, 11 replay as 10, 11, 9, resurrecting an endpoint after retirement. API and client independently consume the durable view. Bypassing the facade leaves the client affected; rolling back the client leaves the facade affected. Correcting replay ordering retains the committed bad view; clearing it alone lets the buggy migration recreate it.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Treating Unimplemented as a wrong rate image or protobuf release
Routing Consul directly to port 8500 and restarting search
Rolling back only the client deployment
Trusting revision 11 as proof retirement revision 10 was applied correctly
Fixing the comparator without rebuilding persisted endpoints
Deleting the snapshot without fixing journal replay
mitigation_summary: Repair the deployed resolver comparator to order revisions numerically, reconstruct the materialized endpoint set from the live journal, and roll search and frontend to refresh connections. No saved baseline or original manifests are needed.

SAYS: The search service is sending rate requests to the geo service, which returns gRPC `Unimplemented` errors. Discovery replay sorts revision numbers as strings, so revision 9 overrides the retirement at revision 10; the resulting bad endpoint list is then cached. I’ll fix the ordering, repair the cached list, and restart search.
